blockNote: Exit-to-world-map actor (Bank 00, 51781-52569). One copy is placed in each of 15 town, village and dungeon-entrance scenes (spawn record x 00, y 01, type 00). It waits for the player to reach a fixed exit zone, then stages the world-map arrival position and a destination-menu id and lets the engine switch to the world map.
=== FLOW ===

1. OverworldExitDispatch compares sceneCurrent with 15 scene ids and JMPs to the region handler. The handler tests the exit zone every frame (South Cape re-enters its own handler with SetEntryHere; all other regions go through the compare chain again each frame).

2. Zone tests: a pixel test on playerYPos (South Cape: Y < $10, Edward's Castle: Y == $2D0) or COP BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles ( minX, minY, maxX, maxY ). The tile test runs on (player X, player Y - 8) and is strict at the minimum edge and inclusive at the maximum edge, in tiles x 16.
3. Inside the zone the handler may test story flags with BranchOnFlagByte. The first flag found set wins, so the later-story flag is tested first where there are two.

4. Every success path does the same: $0D60 := 0, COP StageWorldMapChoice ( start X, start Y, choice id ), JMP OverworldExitFinalize. StageWorldMapChoice only writes worldMapStagedX/PlayerY/ChoiceId; a nonzero staged X makes CheckSceneTransition send the game to scene $FE (the world map). WorldMapController then drops the player at the staged position and runs world_map_options[choice] (a 'Quit / destination' menu).
5. OverworldExitFinalize sets gfxCacheIdxB := $0400, SetEntryHere and RTL: the actor then idles at the RTL until the scene changes.
=== EXITS ===
Choice ids select the menu text in world_map_options (39 entries; ids $01-$1B are staged here). The flag setters are the first match found by searching extracted/ for SetFlagByte.

=== QUIRKS ===
- Edward's Castle compares playerYPos with == $2D0, not a range. If the player can skip that row the exit never fires; not checked (OQ-I042-5).

- The Itory Village exit is disabled while flag $01 is set. $01 is set by unrelated scripts (angel_village, undersea_tunnel, great_wall floor buttons); whether it is cleared on scene load was not traced (OQ-I042-7).

- $0D60 is cleared on every path. It is the first word of the six-word companion array at $0D60-$0D6A that WorldMapController scans to place companion dots; why only the first word is cleared is not known (OQ-I042-6).
- The old header said the actor 'zeroes $0D60, stages the cursor and falls through to the exit handler'; that is right, but the handlers do not 'fall through': they JMP to OverworldExitFinalize.

blockNote: Item-effect sparkle actor (Bank 00, 56579-56667). One spawn is a 24-frame effect that draws two small tiles side by side at the actor's position: 8 frames standing still, then 16 frames rising one pixel per frame. The old text ('four tile entries flanking the hit position', 'spawned during inventory-screen hit feedback') is wrong: it writes two compose-buffer entries per frame and its only spawn site is GiveItemToPlayer.
=== SPAWN ===

inventory_mgmt.GiveItemToPlayer, special-item branch: effect index >= 6 (item id $86 and up) adds 5 to hpToHeal, runs COP SpawnListAppend ( @SpawnHitSparkSprites, #00, #00, #$2F00 ) after PHD / TXA / TCD, then plays sound #22. The fourth operand is the flags word for the child's $10. The child copies position from the actor whose slot is in X when the item is given (the in-line comment there says the player; not verified). No item id of $86 or more was found in the chest tables or GiveItem operands of extracted/, so whether this path is reachable in the shipped game is open (OQ-I042-1).
=== BODY ===

SpawnHitSparkSprites: LoopStart #08 (8 frames) calling AppendHitSparkOamEntry, then LoopStart #10 (16 frames) that first subtracts 1 from $16 and then calls it again; LoopEnd yields every iteration; then Die. There is no initial Y offset (unlike the damage numbers).

AppendHitSparkOamEntry writes two 6-byte entries at the compose-buffer cursor oamWriteOffset ($00D8) in the buffer at $7F3100: X - 4 with tile word $327A, and X + 4 with tile word $327B, both at Y = $16. The tile words are tile $7A and $7B with attribute $3200 (the same priority 3 / palette 1 as the damage digits; tiles $70-$79 are the digits). The cursor advances by $0C. No terminator is written here; the main loop writes $FF after all actors have run.
What tiles $7A / $7B look like was not checked (OQ-I042-2).

SpawnHitSparkSprites: Child actor entry: 8 frames at the spawn position, then 16 frames moving up one pixel per frame, calling AppendHitSparkOamEntry each frame.
AppendHitSparkOamEntry: Append two compose-buffer entries (X - 4 / tile $327A and X + 4 / tile $327B, both at Y = $16) at oamWriteOffset, then oamWriteOffset += $0C. Preserves X.

56579.text: 8 frames standing at the spawn position

56585.text: Yield one frame; repeat until 8 frames are done

56601.text: Yield one frame; repeat until 16 frames are done

56605.text: Save the actor slot (X is the buffer offset below)

blockNote: Floor button (Bank 00, 51710-51778): a solid, hit-triggered switch that raises one numbered event flag each time it is struck. It is not a pressure plate: the actor is solid (MarkSolidHere), so the player cannot stand on it, and the trigger is the engine's hit callback. The old text ('triggers puzzle state when the player or objects land on the plate', 'used in pyramid puzzle rooms') is wrong.
=== INIT ===

actor-def <#00,#00,#01>. $24 := $0E (spawn type byte >> 1, the flag number), then $0E := $2000 (OAM attribute word, priority 2). statsPtr points at enemy_stats_table + $118 (the assembler's offset is hex), which is entry $46: HP $14, ATK $16, DEF $FF, type 0; the actor's currentHp is overwritten with $FF anyway. Metasprite spriteset_enemies, frame $0F shown with AnimOnce, MarkSolidHere. $12 |= $0031: bit $0001 selects between the two post-hit invulnerability modes ($FFEF recovery vs $0011 invincibility in combat_collision; which one it picks was not traced), bit $0010 makes the victim stagger-immune, bit $0020 marks it as a boss so no damage digits are spawned (combat_collision).
loc_00CA1F (re-arm): currentHp := $FF, COP SetHitCallback ( &FloorButtonHitCallback ), SetEntryHere, RTL. The actor then idles.
=== WHEN HIT ===

combat_collision dispatches onHitCallback ($7F1000) after the hit damage: the callback pointer becomes the victim's entry address and onHitCallback is cleared, so the script below runs on the actor's next turn. FloorButtonHitCallback: SetFlagRaw with A = $24 (the event-flag number, no base offset), frame $10 (assumed to be the pressed look; not viewed), AnimOnce, WaitByte #0F, frame $0F, AnimOnce, then BRA loc_00CA1F which restores HP $FF and registers the callback again. The button can therefore be struck again after about $0F frames plus two animation cycles.
=== PLACEMENT AND FLAG READERS ===
Seven spawns, all in Great Wall scenes (the old docs say pyramid):
| Scene | Area | Position (tile) | Type byte | Flag | Reader of that flag |
| 83 | great_wall/wall_dive | 35,1B | 03 | $01 | gw83_switch (WaitOnFlagByte $01, placed on the same tile) |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 18,1A | 03 | $01 | gw85_retractable_gate |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 3B,29 and 29,2B | 05 | $02 | gw85_short_switch_spear |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 37,2C | 07 | $03 | gw85_long_switch_spear |
| 85 | great_wall/wall_rampway | 64,1D | 09 | $04 | gw85_multi_switch_spear |
| 87 | scene 87 (no area folder in extracted/) | 2F,28 | 1F | $0F | none in the scene's spawn list |

The gw85 actors run WaitOnFlagByte ( #n, #01 ) followed by ClearFlagByte ( #n ), so in the rampway the flag is a one-shot trigger consumed by the gate or spear. gw83_switch waits on flag $01 and does not clear it. In scene 87 the flag $0F has no waiter among the scene's actors (the gw82_wall_spear actors it spawns use timers only); $0F is also used as an unrelated flag in Babel Tower and Freejia scripts (OQ-I042-3).
